author: William Shakespeare

findings.lesson_text: Friar Lawrence's herb speech is quoted as: "Within the infant rind of this small flower / Poison hath residence and medicine power."
findings.issue: The adjective in the Friar's herb speech is wrong. The lesson uses "small flower" but the correct Shakespearean text (Act 2, Scene 3) uses "weak flower". "Weak" reinforces the frailty-yet-power duality that is central to the speech's meaning; substituting "small" changes the connotation and will cause students to reproduce the wrong word in closed-book exams.
findings.canonical_truth: Friar Lawrence's exact line (Act 2, Scene 3, Folger edition): "Within the infant rind of this weak flower / Poison hath residence, and medicine power." The adjective "weak" emphasises the flower's apparent fragility contrasted with its hidden potency — a key analytical point. All other boards' versions of this lesson (AQA L3 c6f60dc8, Eduqas L3 e12f8c6a, OCR) correctly quote "weak flower".

audit_notes: All 33 lessons were fetched from Supabase (content_html) and audited in full.
Fact sheet built from RSC scene-by-scene synopsis, Folger full text, NoSweat Shakespeare quote list, and Shakespeare Navigator scene summaries.

Verified: all 15+ major quote attributions (speaker + act/scene) are correct across all 33 lessons — including 'wherefore art thou' (Juliet 2.2), 'yonder window breaks' (Romeo 2.2), 'plague o both your houses' (Mercutio 3.1), 'violent delights' (Friar 2.6), 'never was a story' (Prince 5.3), 'parting is such sweet sorrow' (Juliet 2.2), 'O happy dagger' (Juliet 5.3), 'fortune's fool' (Romeo 3.1), 'defy you stars' (Romeo 5.1).

Verified: all major plot events are correctly sequenced — ball (1.5), balcony (2.2), secret wedding (2.6), Mercutio killed by Tybalt under Romeo's arm (3.1), Romeo kills Tybalt (3.1), banishment (3.1), Juliet refuses Paris (3.5), Friar's potion plan (4.1), Juliet takes potion (4.3), letter fails due to plague quarantine via Friar John (5.2), Romeo kills Paris at tomb (5.3), Romeo drinks poison (5.3), Juliet stabs herself with dagger (5.3).

Verified: all character identities and relationships are correct — Mercutio as Prince's kinsman (not Montague), Juliet as 13 years old, Friar Lawrence as Romeo's confessor, Balthasar as Romeo's servant who brings news, Friar John as the letter-carrier quarantined.
Verified: Juliet's death method is consistently and correctly stated as a dagger (not poison) across all 33 lessons.

Verified: the shared sonnet at the ball (Act 1 Scene 5) is correctly attributed and its structure (Romeo Q1, Juliet Q2, shared Q3 and couplet) is accurately described in the OCR/Eduqas language lessons.

Minor variation noted but not flagged as error: AQA L10 (86391034) gives the play's compressed timeline as 'five days'; OCR L7 (39ec45f4) and others say 'approximately four days'. Both are defensible scholarly positions.
